newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada cuts key rate to 3.75 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada cuts key rate to 3.75 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Canada on Wednesday lowered its key bank rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.75 percent, bringing interest rates in Canada to their lowest level in almost 40 years.
The cut came on the heels of a series of weak economic statistics accompanied by a stronger Canadian dollar in the past few weeks.
The rate reduction quickly prompted Canada's six big chartered banks to lower their prime lending rates to 5.25 percent from 5.50 percent, the lowest level since early 1959.

It was the ninth rate cut by Canada's central bank this year and the eighth independent of an easing by the U.S. Federal Reserve. The Bank of Canada has now eased by 4.50 percentage points since May 1995. Its previous rate cut was on Oct. 2.
The bank rate is the top of the central bank's target range for the overnight rate, at which it lends to financial institutions in its role as lender of last resort.
The Canadian dollar, T-bills and bonds firmed after the rate cut.
The Bank of Canada said the rate cut was designed to keep monetary conditions from tightening.
"Given a stronger Canadian dollar, this action was designed to keep overall monetary conditions from tightening," the Bank said.
The easing had been widely expected following last Friday's Statistics Canada report that unemployment in Canada jumped to 9.9 percent in September from 9.4 percent in August.

A report released earlier on Wednesday showing a decline in manufacturers' shipments and new orders and an increase in inventories in August confirmed speculation that Canada's economic recovery is weak.
